Diamond cut grades `measure how well a diamond's facets interact with light` , graded on a standard five-point scale from Excellent to Poor.[[1]](https://www.tiffany.com/engagement/diamond-education/cut.html)[[2]](https://www.revediamonds.com/us/diamond-cut-grading)

### The GIA Cut Grading Scale

The [Gemological Institute of America (GIA)](https://www.gia.edu/gia-about/4cs-cut) uses the most widely accepted scale for standard round brilliant diamonds:

- **Excellent:** Reflects nearly all incoming light, creating exceptional brilliance and sparkle.
- **Very Good:** Reflects most light; offers great quality and appearance at a lower price than Excellent.
- **Good:** Reflects a majority of light, though some brilliance may be lost to save carat weight.
- **Fair:** Allows significant light to escape through the sides or bottom; appears less lively.
- **Poor:** Lets most light escape, resulting in a dull, lifeless stone.

### How Cut is Evaluated

- **Brightness:** Total white light reflected from and within the diamond.
- **Fire:** The dispersion of light into rainbow spectrum colors.
- **Scintillation:** The pattern of light, dark areas, and sparkle when the stone moves.
- **Polish & Symmetry:** The precision of the facet shapes and how smoothly they are finished.[[1]](https://www.gia.edu/gia-about/4cs-cut)[[2]](https://4cs.gia.edu/en-us/blog/gia-diamond-cut-grade-six-things-to-know/)
